reason: The cited evidence shows that Al addition can reduce density and retain BCC structure in other refractory high-entropy alloys (E2, E3), but none of the passages involve the HfMoTaTiZr system or demonstrate that Al substitution for Hf preserves strength at both room temperature and ~1000 °C. E1 discusses HfMoTaTiZr but without Al, so the key premises about strength retention and phase stability in this specific system are unsupported.
premises: Partial substitution of Hf with Al reduces density
BCC single-phase structure is retained after Al addition
Room-temperature strength is maintained after Al substitution
High-temperature strength (~1000 °C) is maintained after Al substitution
Solid-solution strengthening from Al addition compensates for Hf removal
